clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying an apple orchard: within the year, June grew homesick and wrote to her sister Edna every day, Walter spent long hours in the trees and grew distant from June, Glen began fighting at his new school, Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, Walter and June rowed over money for new trees, and by September June had joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out. The shifts pile up from May 1952 through September 1953 as the family settled into the orchard and the valley.

clusters.name: the orchard's failure, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: within months, Walter drank heavily most nights, he and Glen blamed each other for the loan, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl developed worse asthma attacks that winter, you began wetting the bed in April 1969, your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working, and Walter stopped drinking by October and took work pruning other men's trees. The shifts show across the family from June 1968 through October 1969 as the orchard sold and the family moved to Ridgeport.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: within months, Glen sat in the truck in the yard for hours out of work, he and Marian fought loudly at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother, Walter drank again after six years without it, and by June 1976 you were eating again and had made the track team. The shifts pile up from May 1975 through June 1976 across the household.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your home, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: within months, you clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice, Wilma took over Lily's care, you developed eczema on both hands, you rowed with Hollis most nights, and your mother drove over twice a week to take your side. Wilma moved to a flat in town in June 1991, and your eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts run from April 1990 through August 1991 as the household settled after Wilma's departure.

declined.reason: 1994: The events of 4–5 August 1994 around the wildfire are an acute episode. The family was ordered to the school gym for three nights, everyone became frightened, the children developed acute anxiety and stomach upset, you and Hollis clashed over driving out, and within days of being allowed home on 15 August you were calm again and the children returned to school. All shifts fall within the same few days around a real threat, and the family settled within a week; this is not a period.
